clue.text: Work out how to effect seizure of donjon?

blocks.note: a donjon is the keep, the central tower of a castle
a fit is a sudden seizure

explanation.surface: A question about how to capture the central tower of a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as a castle tower having a fit: the seizure belongs to the donjon, so the tower word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep fit is to exercise regularly, which is what working out at a gym means.

clue.text: See 27
Improve and ruin English Channel, nearly

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck its shape, so the letters are scrambled into a new order
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word before it is dropped

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
the word channel with its final letter removed

explanation.surface: A complaint that some scheme meant to improve the English Channel has ruined it instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to make it better, raising its quality or value.

clue.text: Sweet and silly?

blocks.note: first meaning: a dessert of puréed fruit folded into cream or custard
second meaning: foolish, as in an informal adjective for a daft idea

explanation.walkthrough: Sweet here is a British word for a dessert; gooseberry fool is the classic example.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is both a creamy fruit pudding and, informally, an adjective for something foolish or daft.

clue.text: 14, one of the 15, and 10's other half were a menace, with me a bonnie mess inside ...

definitions.text: 14, one of the 15, and 10's other half

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder
inside tells us that the jumbled letters sit within the menace word

blocks.note: a menace is a threat
taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Three cross-referenced characters made a nuisance of themselves, with the speaker caught up in a muddle among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is JEROME, 15 the GEORGES, and 10 is LEWIS, whose other half is Harris, as in the Scottish island Lewis and Harris. Jerome, George and Harris are Jerome K. Jerome's THREE MEN IN A BOAT, with the jumble sitting inside THREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel follows the narrator J., his friend George and Harris on a rowing trip up the Thames.

clue.text: Plain cake saw?

definitions.note: read as two words: a cake that has no icing

blocks.note: first meaning, split into two words: a cake without any icing on top
second meaning: spotted or observed

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as NOT ICED, which describes a plain cake; read whole, it is a past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Saw in the past tense means observed or spotted something, the same sense as having noticed it.

clue.text: In a supermarket the French film is invisible to the naked eye

indicators.note: in places the French article within the supermarket name

blocks.note: Tesco is a British supermarket chain
le is French for the
pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: Something filmed inside a supermarket that nobody could actually see.
explanation.definitionFit: Telescopic objects, such as distant stars, can be seen only through a telescope, not by the unaided eye.

clue.text: Pat's constituent reportedly intimidated and suspended?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is told, so we go by how the following words are spoken

blocks.note: cowed means intimidated and hung means suspended; run together they sound like the answer

explanation.surface: A man called Pat felt bullied and was then suspended from office.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat looks like a person's name, but it is a cowpat, a flat lump of cattle dung.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowpat is made of cattle droppings, so the dung is what the pat consists of.

clue.text: They sleep rough, so dress is a problem

indicators.note: if the words are a problem, they are in trouble and get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Homeless people sleeping outdoors struggle to find decent clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dossers is British slang for vagrants who doss, sleeping wherever they can, often on the street.

clue.text: A month without choral work, he'd like the mob to rule

definitions.text: he'd like the mob to rule

indicators.note: work here means to work over, reshaping the letters of the word before it
without in its old sense of outside means the month surrounds the other letters

blocks.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who goes a month without singing in the choir and fancies mob rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without choral work' reads as going without music, but without means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: An ochlocrat is an advocate of ochlocracy, government by the mob or the masses.

clue.text: Snowman, as it were, in the French fashion, to work the other way

indicators.note: the other way means running in the opposite direction, so the work word is read back to front

blocks.note: le is French for the
wise is an old word for way or manner, as in 'in this wise'
to toil is to work hard

explanation.surface: Building a snowman the French way, by working in the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snowman' is not a figure of snow but a man created by C. P. Snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Eliot is the narrator of C. P. Snow's novel sequence Strangers and Brothers, so he is Snow's man.

clue.text: Pieces of second-hand quartz?

blocks.note: surface reading: bits of a used quartz crystal or a pre-owned quartz watch
setter's reading: tiny grains of quartz worn down from older rock, so recycled by nature

explanation.walkthrough: Second-hand suggests a quartz watch's second hand; in fact the grains are quartz that has been weathered from rock already used once.
explanation.definitionFit: Beach sand consists largely of fine quartz grains broken down from older rocks over time.

clue.text: Novelist wrote bad things before residence in Tyneside

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair of words within the region's abbreviation

blocks.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
evils are bad things
a hut is a humble dwelling

explanation.surface: A writer produced nasty stuff before moving to Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevil Shute was an English-born novelist, author of A Town Like Alice and On the Beach.

clue.text: Quadruped's need of food: true? False

definitions.note: possessive noun standing for an adjective meaning of or like a quadruped

indicators.note: false means untrue to the original, so the letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A quiz question: is it true that an animal needs food? False.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadruped is an animal with four feet, so its quality is being four-footed.

clue.text: Bible translator, the first person in French and Latin city

blocks.note: je is French for I, the first person pronoun
Rome was the city of the Latin-speaking Romans

explanation.surface: Introducing a Bible translator who leads a list of French and Latin names.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Jerome produced the Vulgate, the Latin translation of the Bible used by the Church for centuries.

clue.text: 19 or 11 and 24 (IV Kings)

blocks.note: first meaning: the first name of the writer at 19, or of the two women novelists at 11 and 24
second meaning: the four Hanoverian kings of Britain who shared one name

explanation.walkthrough: IV Kings looks like a Bible book reference, but it means the four Hanoverian kings who shared a name. 19 is SIMENON, 11 is SAND and 24 is ELIOT; two of those are women writing under a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon, George Sand, George Eliot and Kings George I to IV all bear this first name.

clue.text: I get a drink when back to fighting Japanese

indicators.note: back means going in reverse, so the whole string is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
rum is a spirit, a drink
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone who has a drink whenever they come home from fighting the Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan, so they were fighting Japanese.

clue.text: Have a meal, eating fish, causing a disturbance

indicators.note: eating means taking something in, so the meal word swallows the fish

blocks.note: to sup is to eat supper
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A diner causes a scene while eating fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is an upheaval or radical reorganisation, a disturbance of the existing order.

clue.text: Island produced a change of air

indicators.note: a change of the word means altering it, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: made means produced
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An island whose climate makes a pleasant change of air for visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic, also famous for its fortified wine.

clue.text: Frail insect eating a single document

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the insect word goes around the rest

blocks.note: a fly is an insect
I is the Roman numeral one
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: A weak insect munching on a lone sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimsy means weak and easily damaged, so something frail could be called flimsy.

clue.text: Writer of detective stories puts people in heaven

indicators.note: puts something in means placing it within the heaven word

blocks.note: Sion, or Zion, is the heavenly city
men are people

explanation.surface: A crime writer sends characters to heaven by killing them off.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon was the Belgian author of the Inspector Maigret detective novels.

clue.text: She was Hectored, with memory suffering

blocks.note: and means together with
ROM is read-only memory in a computer
an ache is a pain, suffering

explanation.surface: A woman was bullied and her memory suffered for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Hectored seems to mean bullied, but with a capital it means married to Hector of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Iliad Andromache is the wife of the Trojan hero Hector, so she belonged to Hector.

clue.text: In the bathroom I try to skip

indicators.note: in says the letters are found lying within the next few words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the next two

explanation.surface: Someone tries to slip out of the bathroom unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, which is what skipping it means.

clue.text: ... not to mention their friend, awful fogy in hat, honest to God!

annotation.answer: TO SAY NOTHING OF THE DOG

indicators.note: awful means in a terrible state, so the following letters are jumbled

blocks.clueFragment: fogy in hat, honest to God
blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing 4: and their companion, a dreadful old fogey in a hat, really and truly.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the subtitle of the novel at 4. 'Not to mention' is a synonym for the phrase's opening words, and their friend is the dog Montmorency.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's full title adds this phrase because the three men take along Montmorency, a fox terrier, as their companion.

clue.text: Eat up, girl!

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A mother urging a child named Enid to finish her food.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a girl's first name, as with the children's writer Enid Blyton.

clue.text: See 10
Seminarians from Breton town dividing gold and diamonds

indicators.note: dividing means splitting something apart, so the town sits between the other pieces

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
Dinan is a town in Brittany
D is the card abbreviation for diamond, made plural

explanation.surface: Trainee priests from a town in Brittany separating out their gold and jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinands are candidates preparing for ordination, which is what students at a seminary are.

clue.text: Approval of archbishop being in hell?

indicators.note: being in puts the churchman inside the hell word

blocks.note: the pit is hell, the bottomless pit
William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: Asking whether anyone approves of an archbishop ending up in hell.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or applause, a mark of approval.

clue.text: What could possibly go with West London sky? I've no idea!

indicators.note: asking what the words could possibly become invites us to try other arrangements

blocks.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for West
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shrugging question about what could match the sky over West London.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an idiom of complete ignorance: nobody but the Almighty has the answer.
